messages.subject: est.map() and mqm
parts:
I have a cross with physical maps and used est.map() to generate an
estimated genetic map. However it seems that the new mqm
functionality doesn't recognize that the baseline values are not
zeroed for the map and still sees it as a physical map.

I was able to correct this by subtracting the first marker location
from the rest. Is this the correct way to do it?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] est.map() and mqm
parts:
It took a while to figure out what you were talking about. It's helpful to get a bit of code and the exact error report.

But I take it that the problem is the following: est.map, by default, keeps the location of the first marker as it was, and so if you start with physical maps in basepairs, the marker positions will all end up on the order of 10^6. mqmscan has an argument step.max, that is the maximum position it considers, and so if this is less than the first marker position, an error is given.

We're working to fix this.

In the development version of R/qtl (see http://www.rqtl.org/download), we have added a couple of tools that will help.

est.map has an argument offset to indicate the starting positions for the chromosomes.

newmap <- est.map(mycross, offset=0)
mycross <- replace.map(mycross, newmap)

Alternatively, we've added a function shiftmap(), which can be used after the fact, either to the map or to the cross:

mycross <- shiftmap(mycross, offset=0)

newmap <- shiftmap(newmap, offset=0)
mycross <- replace.map(mycross, newmap)

I hope to release a new version of R/qtl within a week or two.

karl
